author: ababushk
title: ARM64 cross-compilation build fails with cc1plus: not a PCH file (invalid-pch) in openvino_reference
signature: cc1plus error cmake_pch hxx gch not a pch file werror invalid pch|Infrastructure

failed_jobs.name: Build / Build
failed_jobs.symptom: CMake configure, build and install step for OpenVINO JS API failed: cc1plus errors that cmake_pch.hxx.gch is not a valid PCH file, treated as -Werror=invalid-pch across src/core/reference

failed_jobs.name: ci/gha_overall_status_ubuntu_22_arm64_cross_compilation
failed_jobs.symptom: Overall status check failed because the upstream Build job failed

key_errors:
FAILED: [code=1] src/core/reference/CMakeFiles/openvino_reference.dir/src/op/convert.cpp.o
cc1plus: error: /__w/openvino/openvino/openvino/openvino_build/src/core/reference/CMakeFiles/openvino_reference.dir/cmake_pch.hxx.gch: not a PCH file [-Werror=invalid-pch]
cc1plus: all warnings being treated as errors
sccache stats: Compile requests 8248, Compile requests executed 8246, Cache hits 8243, Cache misses 0 (abnormally close to 100% hit rate just before the PCH errors begin)
root_cause: The precompiled header (cmake_pch.hxx.gch) for the openvino_reference target was retrieved from sccache in a corrupted or incompatible form (stale/incomplete cache entry, likely from a prior run's partially-written or cross-run-incompatible PCH artifact), so when GCC's cc1plus tried to consume it, it rejected it as 'not a PCH file'. Because the build uses -Werror=invalid-pch, this diagnostic is escalated to a hard build failure. This is the third recorded occurrence of the identical cc1plus/PCH signature on this ARM64 cross-compilation workflow (previously seen 2026-09-24/25, affecting different source files each time but the same openvino_reference/other core targets), strongly indicating a flaky/corrupted sccache artifact issue rather than a code defect — this PR's changes (Bandit nosec annotations in Python CI scripts and a docker_tag string) do not touch any C++ source, build flags, or PCH configuration.
